subject: science
title: The Drum's Sound
objective: Describe how a drum makes sound when struck and how to protect our ears.
introduction: Milo strikes a drum and hears a sound. What vibrates, and how can Maxine protect her ears?

vocabulary.definition: A quick back-and-forth movement that can make sound.
A vibration that travels through air or another material to your ears.
Ways to protect your ears from sounds that are too loud.

items.prompt: Milo strikes a drum. What makes the sound?
items.explanation: Striking makes the drum skin vibrate, and that vibration makes sound. A sponge, towel, or pillow does not vibrate like the drum skin here.

items.prompt: Maxine practices drumming. Which choice protects her hearing?

options.text: Move away from very loud sound

items.explanation: Very loud sound can hurt ears, so moving away reduces the sound reaching them. Quiet unrelated actions do not make loud practice safer.

items.prompt: Milo reads four safety claims. Which action is NOT safe?

options.text: Put a speaker beside an ear
Take a break from loud sound

items.explanation: A speaker beside an ear can damage hearing. Lower volume, breaks, and moving away reduce the risk from loud sound.

items.prompt: Maxine strikes a drum and feels the top shake. Which example shows how sound behaves?

options.text: A lamp lights a dark room
A drum skin vibrates and makes sound

items.explanation: The struck drum skin vibrates and moves air, producing sound. Lamps, mirrors, and flashlights are about light.

items.prompt: Milo hears a drum during practice. Which choice shows safe listening?

options.text: Bang the drum beside a baby
Turn the volume all the way up
Strike as hard as possible for hours
Use a safe volume and take breaks

items.explanation: A safe volume and breaks give ears time away from harmful loudness. Very loud, close, or nonstop sound can hurt hearing.
